concepts.name: Definition and Classification of Urban Agglomerations (UA) by Census of India
key_dimensions: Census of India's three-fold criteria: a city/town + outgrowths OR two or more contiguous towns
Distinction between UA, statutory town, census town, and outgrowth — UPSC trap on overlapping definitions
Minimum population threshold (100,000+) for UA classification vs. town classification (5,000+)
Why a UA may span multiple districts or states — administrative vs. functional urban boundary

concepts.name: Million-Plus Urban Agglomerations in India: Growth Trends and Distribution
key_dimensions: Number of million-plus UAs across Census 2001, 2011 — increase from 35 to 53
Spatial concentration: dominance of Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, UP — regional imbalance angle
Primate city vs. rank-size rule applicability to Indian million-plus cities
Functional classification of million-plus UAs: industrial, service, administrative — UPSC map-based question angle

concepts.name: Megacities vs. Meta-cities: Concept and Indian Examples
key_dimensions: Megacity threshold (10 million+) vs. meta-city (20 million+) — definitional precision trap
Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata positioning in global megacity rankings and their trajectory
Distinction between megacity as a statistical unit vs. a governance/planning unit
Global South megacity challenges: infrastructure deficit, informality, ecological footprint

concepts.name: Urban Primacy and the Primate City Concept in Indian Context
key_dimensions: Mark Jefferson's law of the primate city — definition and applicability
India's partial primacy: Mumbai and Delhi as dual primate cities — exception to the classic model
Primacy index calculation and comparison with rank-size rule (Zipf's Law)
Policy implications: over-concentration of economic activity and regional inequality

concepts.name: Rank-Size Rule (Zipf's Law) and Its Applicability to Indian Urban System
key_dimensions: Zipf's Law formulation: population of nth city = population of largest city / n
India's urban hierarchy deviating from perfect rank-size distribution — reasons and implications
Comparison: USA (near rank-size conformity) vs. India (partial primacy pattern)
Policy relevance: balanced regional development and counter-magnet city strategy

concepts.name: Concept of Conurbation, Megalopolis, and Ecumenopolis
key_dimensions: Conurbation (Patrick Geddes): merging of originally separate towns — UK examples vs. Indian applicability
Megalopolis (Jean Gottmann): Boston–Washington corridor concept and emerging Indian corridors (Delhi–Meerut, Mumbai–Pune)
Ecumenopolis: hypothetical continuous world city — theoretical vs. practical relevance
UPSC trap: distinguishing conurbation from UA and metropolitan area definitionally

concepts.name: Metropolitan Region vs. Urban Agglomeration: Administrative and Functional Boundaries
key_dimensions: UA as a Census concept vs. Metropolitan Region as a planning/governance concept
National Capital Region (NCR) as India's largest planning metropolitan region — multi-state spread
Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), Chennai Metropolitan Area — governance body vs. Census UA mismatch
74th Constitutional Amendment and Metropolitan Planning Committees (MPCs) for cities 10 lakh+ — implementation gap

concepts.name: Causes of Urban Agglomeration: Agglomeration Economies and Push-Pull Factors
key_dimensions: Agglomeration economies: localization (same industry clustering) vs. urbanization economies (diverse industries)
Rural push factors: agricultural distress, landlessness, climate vulnerability
Urban pull factors: employment, services, infrastructure — differential pull across city sizes
Circuit of capital and cumulative causation (Myrdal's backwash effect) sustaining agglomeration growth

concepts.name: Urban Sprawl vs. Compact City Growth in Indian Agglomerations
key_dimensions: Urban sprawl definition: low-density, automobile-dependent outward expansion — Bengaluru, Hyderabad case
Peri-urbanization: transitional rural-urban fringe areas with mixed land use — Census classification challenge
Compact city model: transit-oriented development (TOD), mixed land use — Smart Cities Mission alignment
Environmental consequences: loss of agricultural land, urban heat island, groundwater depletion

concepts.name: Outgrowths and Peri-Urban Areas: Definition, Classification Challenges
key_dimensions: Census definition of outgrowth: railway colony, university campus, port area contiguous to a town
Peri-urban areas: neither fully rural nor urban — governance vacuum and service delivery challenge
Undercounting of urban population due to delayed reclassification of peri-urban areas
UPSC trap: outgrowth classified as part of UA but not as a separate town — double-counting risk

concepts.name: Infrastructure Challenges in Urban Agglomerations: Housing, Water, Sanitation
key_dimensions: Housing shortage: EWS/LIG deficit — PMAY Urban targets vs. ground reality in mega-UAs
Water stress in agglomerations: Chennai, Bengaluru water crisis — groundwater over-extraction
Solid waste management: Municipal Solid Waste Rules 2016, Swachh Bharat Mission Urban metrics
Informal settlements (slums) as a structural feature of Indian UAs — Dharavi redevelopment as case study

concepts.name: Governance of Urban Agglomerations: Fragmentation and the 74th Amendment
key_dimensions: 74th Constitutional Amendment: 18 functions in 12th Schedule, Ward Committees, MPCs — mandatory vs. optional provisions trap
Governance fragmentation: multiple agencies (NMMC, MCGM, CIDCO in Mumbai) with overlapping jurisdictions
State reluctance to empower urban local bodies — devolution index findings
Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) under Smart Cities Mission bypassing elected ULBs — democratic deficit debate

concepts.name: Economic Geography of Urban Agglomerations: Industrial and Service Clusters
key_dimensions: Sectoral specialization of Indian UAs: Mumbai (finance/services), Chennai (auto hub), Bengaluru (IT), Surat (textiles/diamonds)
Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and industrial corridors as planned agglomeration drivers — DMIC, CBIC
Informal economy's dominance in UA employment — NSSO/PLFS data on self-employment in cities
Knowledge economy and talent concentration: brain drain from small cities to mega-UAs

concepts.name: Urban Heat Island (UHI) Effect in Large Agglomerations
key_dimensions: Mechanism: impervious surfaces, waste heat, reduced vegetation elevating temperatures 2–5°C above surroundings
Consequences: increased energy demand, heat stress mortality, altered local precipitation patterns
Mitigation strategies: urban greening, cool roofs, reflective pavements — relevance to climate action plans
UPSC linkage: UHI as intersection of urbanisation, climate change, public health, and urban planning

concepts.name: Migration Patterns Feeding Urban Agglomerations: Types and Trends
key_dimensions: Step migration theory vs. direct rural-to-mega-city migration in India — Census 2011 migration data
Circular migration: seasonal, footloose migrants not fully captured in Census UA population counts
Inter-state vs. intra-state migration flows — UP, Bihar as source states; Maharashtra, Delhi, Gujarat as destination UAs
Feminisation of migration: increasing female migration to UAs for domestic work, garment industry

concepts.name: Smart Cities Mission and Its Relationship with Urban Agglomerations
key_dimensions: SCM focus on Area-Based Development (ABD) within cities — critique of island development vs. whole-city approach
100 Smart Cities selection criteria — competition-based selection, not based on UA size or need
SPV model, convergence with AMRUT, PMAY — institutional overlaps and coordination failures
Digital infrastructure (ICCC) in smart cities vs. basic service deficits in peripheral UA areas — equity paradox

concepts.name: Demographic Dividend and Urban Agglomerations as Engines of Growth
key_dimensions: Urban areas contributing ~60–65% of India's GDP despite housing ~35% of population — productivity differential
Young migrant population in UAs: demographic dividend realization contingent on urban job creation
Agglomeration and innovation: density-driven knowledge spillovers — Bengaluru tech ecosystem as example
Risk of demographic dividend reversal: urban unemployment, skill mismatch in manufacturing-weak UAs

concepts.name: Slums within Urban Agglomerations: Census Definition, Distribution, and Policy
key_dimensions: Census 2011: 65.49 million slum population; slum as 'notified', 'recognized', or 'identified' — three-category distinction
Spatial distribution: Mumbai (largest slum population), Visakhapatnam (highest % urban population in slums) — map trap
In-situ slum upgrading (Rajiv AwasYojana legacy) vs. resettlement — policy debate and community resistance
Slums as informal economic hubs: Dharavi's $1 billion informal economy — policy reframing

concepts.name: Counter-Magnet Cities and Satellite Towns as Decongestion Strategies
key_dimensions: Counter-magnet city concept: developing secondary cities to absorb migration pressure from megacities
JNNURM/AMRUT focus on Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities as policy instrument for balanced urbanisation
Satellite towns vs. new towns: Navi Mumbai (planned new town) vs. Gurgaon (organic satellite) — comparison
Failure factors: lack of employment base, poor connectivity, inadequate social infrastructure in planned satellites

concepts.name: Urban Agglomerations and Environmental Sustainability: Ecological Footprint and Resilience
key_dimensions: Ecological footprint of mega-UAs: per capita resource consumption vs. rural areas — resource hinterland dependency
Urban flooding in agglomerations: Chennai 2015, Mumbai 2005 — concretisation, encroachment on wetlands and floodplains
Urban biodiversity and green infrastructure: role of urban forests, lakes in UA resilience — Bengaluru's vanishing lakes
Sendai Framework, urban resilience, and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) planning for high-density UAs
